audit.whatIsWrong: `wants.you[1]` tells Mel to 'sprint out of her tentacle field' after Test of Spirit lands, and `mid` says she is 'forced to run from your own shadow'. Running is presented as the answer.
audit.why: Riot's own text for Test of Spirit: 'If killed, or if the target gets too far from the spirit, the target will become a Vessel and begin spawning Tentacles.' Running away from the torn spirit is the single action that converts Mel into a Vessel. The current advice actively causes the loss condition it is warning about.
audit.corrected: Once the spirit is out, stay inside its leash and out of tentacle range and let it expire. Do not run, and do not let it be killed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere warns that Mel's own area damage can hit her torn spirit.
audit.why: Test of Spirit spirits 'echo a percentage of the damage they take to the original target'. Radiant Volley is a zone that explodes around a target location, and the spirit stands next to Illaoi — so a Mel who keeps Qing Illaoi after eating E is echoing her own barrage back into herself. This is the highest-value hidden interaction in the matchup and Mel is unusually exposed to it because her only poke is an AoE.
audit.corrected: After Test of Spirit lands, check where your spirit is standing before you throw Radiant Volley.

audit.whatIsWrong: full `tldr` reads 'He can't reach you and you reflect what he throws'.
audit.why: Three separate errors in one line. Illaoi is female and the rest of this entry uses she/her. Harsh Lesson is a 400-range leap on a flat 4-second cooldown, so she reaches Mel constantly. And Illaoi's kit carries no projectile flag at all — Rebuttal has nothing to reflect here, which is precisely why this matchup is hard for Mel and not easy.
audit.corrected: She closes with Harsh Lesson every 4s and Rebuttal has no projectile to return; the lane is won on spacing, not on reflect.

audit.whatIsWrong: `spikes[0]` and `early` place Mel's Q poke at 550 range.
audit.why: Radiant Volley's range is 950. 550 is Mel's basic-attack range. Against a champion whose only gap-close is a 400-range leap, the 400-unit difference between 550 and 950 is the whole early game.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer grades this FAVOURED at 4/10 with Mel winning all seven phases; the content layer says 'this is where you lose the lane' and gives Illaoi 4 of 7. Mel's win rate is 42.86%.
audit.why: The two layers state opposite conclusions and the optimistic one contradicts the data. A losing win rate cannot be a 4/10 favoured lane, and the phase whys under side='Mel' are generic Mel-positive boilerplate rather than anything about Illaoi.
audit.corrected: Grade the lane HARD at 6/10 and align the full phases with the content chart (Illaoi from level 3 through first item).

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds even though it repeatedly complains that Illaoi heals the chip back.
audit.why: Prophet of an Elder God heals Illaoi whenever her Tentacles damage a champion, which is the mechanism behind every 'she heals it back' line already in the text. The full layer's itemization block already calls for early anti-heal; the content layer never does, so the player is told the problem without the item that solves it.
audit.corrected: Name Grievous Wounds in the early-game plan.

audit.whatIsWrong: full `breakdown.cooldowns` says to track Test of Spirit but gives no number, and ignores Harsh Lesson entirely.
audit.why: Test of Spirit is 16/15/14/13/12s — a long, countable window. Harsh Lesson is a flat 4s, which is the reason Mel can never treat 400 range as safe. Both numbers change how a player walks.
audit.corrected: State 16s at rank 1 falling to 12s, and flag Harsh Lesson's flat 4s.

notes: Two things I did NOT act on. (1) champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json claims 'Illaoi can go untargetable through your commit (Leap of Faith (R))'. Riot's own description text for Leap of Faith says nothing about untargetability, so this comes from a derived flag I cannot confirm — I left it out rather than tell a player to hold burst for a window that may not exist. Worth verifying on the League Wiki before anyone writes it in. (2) The full layer refers to Illaoi as 'he/him' throughout (tldr, winCon, enemyWin, wave, feeding, common mistakes, all-in windows). I corrected only the tldr; the rest looks like a champion-agnostic template applied across many matchups and is better fixed at the generator than one string at a time. The full `diff` edit ('FAVOURED' -> 'HARD') and the four phases[].side edits change short enum labels and cannot satisfy the +/-10% band; they are recorded in the audit above so the finding survives if the applier rejects them.

edits.before: Your 550-range Q poke and Searing Brilliance autos chunk her before she has tentacles or sustain — your only clean window.
edits.after: Radiant Volley's 950 range and Searing Brilliance autos chunk her before any tentacle or Vessel heal exists — your one window.

edits.before: Once her E (Test of Spirit) and a tentacle field are up, every Q you throw heals her back and her vessel-smacks shred your squishy frame.
edits.after: Once Test of Spirit (E) is up, any Radiant Volley that clips your own torn spirit echoes a share of that damage straight back onto you.

edits.before: Illaoi R + Leap of Faith spawns a wall of tentacles — getting caught in the field with no dash is a guaranteed death for you.
edits.after: Leap of Faith (R) spawns one tentacle per champion it hits — caught in that field with no dash, you simply do not walk out.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are the only part of this lane that belongs to you. Sit at 550 range, Q the wave-and-Illaoi overlap, and use your Searing Brilliance empowered autos to stack Overwhelm and chunk her before she has a tentacle field built. At level 2 your Q-plus-Solar Snare can land a real punish if she steps up for a tentacle slam on the wave. But the second her E (Test of Spirit) and a couple tentacles are online, the math flips hard — every poke you throw, she heals back off vessel slams, and your squishy frame can't trade into that sustain.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are the only part of this lane that belongs to you. Sit at Radiant Volley's 950 range, Q the wave-and-Illaoi overlap, and use your Searing Brilliance empowered autos to stack Overwhelm before she has a tentacle field built. At level 2 your Q-plus-Solar Snare can land a real punish if she steps up for a tentacle slam on the wave. But the second Test of Spirit and a couple of tentacles are online the math flips hard — every tentacle that connects with a champion heals her, so buy Grievous Wounds early or your chip just refunds itself.

edits.before: This is where you lose the lane. By level 3-5 her tentacle field out-sustains your entire poke pattern, and if her E rips your spirit you're forced to run from your own shadow while her tentacles chase. At 6 her Leap of Faith spawns a wall of slams — with zero dashes and only one CC, getting caught in that field is just death. Hold Solar Snare (E) purely as an escape tool, not engage: snare the ground to peel a tentacle leap and sprint out, and never walk up to Q if her R is up.
edits.after: This is where you lose the lane. By 3-5 her tentacle field out-sustains your whole poke pattern and Harsh Lesson leaps 400 units onto you every 4 seconds. If Test of Spirit rips your spirit, do NOT sprint away — leaving it, or letting it die, is exactly what turns you into a Vessel. Stay inside its leash, out of tentacle reach, and wait it out. At 6 Leap of Faith spawns a wall of slams; with zero dashes and one CC, getting caught in that field is just death. Hold Solar Snare as peel, never as engage.

edits.before: Land Solar Snare (E) the instant she casts her E spirit-tear so you can sprint out of her tentacle field
edits.after: After Test of Spirit lands, stay inside leash range of your spirit — running out of it is what makes you a Vessel

edits.before: With her E and a tentacle field online, every Q you throw heals her off vessel slams and your trades stop working.
edits.after: With Test of Spirit up, a Radiant Volley that clips your own torn spirit echoes that damage back onto you — reposition first.

edits.before: He can't reach you and you reflect what he throws — stack Overwhelm on every step-up and execute at 6.
edits.after: She leaps 400 onto you every 4s and Rebuttal has nothing to reflect — this lane is spacing, not poke.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse online — anyone you've stacked is now walking around with a countdown. Chip, stack, execute.
edits.after: Level 6 is hers, not yours — Leap of Faith spawns a tentacle per champion hit and you have no way out of it.

edits.before: - Illaoi Test of Spirit: matchup-defining — Dodging the spirit pull is the entire matchup. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Rebuttal like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Illaoi Test of Spirit: 16s at rank 1, down to 12s at rank 5 — that gap is your only safe step-up. - Harsh Lesson is a flat 4s, so she is never truly out of range. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
